title: Elon Musk teases a Warren Buffett-style pledge to give his money away
excerpt: Elon Musk hinted at a Warren Buffett-style commitment after a Nobel economist challenged him over his prediction that "money won't matter" by 2036.
content_html:
By Theron Mohamed

You're currently following this author! Want to unfollow? Unsubscribe via the link in your email.

Is Elon Musk about to give us his best impression of Warren Buffett?

The Tesla and SpaceX CEO has teased that he may pledge some of his fortune to good causes, to show he truly believes that technology will create such abundance that money will become irrelevant.

Musk raised the prospect after Nobel economist Daron Acemoglu, responding to Musk's prediction of a post-wealth world in a recent interview, proposed an "opportunity to put your money where your mouth is."

"If money won't matter in 2036, why don't you pledge to donate your current wealth of approximately $1 trillion to charity no later than 2036," the veteran MIT professor wrote.

Acemoglu said that doing so would "establish with great credibility" Musk's belief in the "powers of AI and technology," and also relieve widespread concern about the "political and social influence of billionaires and trillionaires."

The post sparked heated debate on X, leading Musk to weigh in a few hours later. "I am actually going to do something along these lines!" he wrote.

I am actually going to do something along these lines!

— Elon Musk (@elonmusk) July 27, 2026

Musk hasn't elaborated on what he's planning. Tesla, SpaceX, and X didn't immediately respond to requests for comment from Business Insider.

Pulling from the Buffett playbook

If Musk pledges to give a chunk of his wealth to charity within the next decade or so, he'll be giving Buffett a run for his money.

Buffett famously co-launched the Giving Pledge in 2010, encouraging other ultra-wealthy people to sign it with him and commit to giving the majority of their wealth to good causes.

The legendary investor and Berkshire Hathaway CEO has gifted about 60% of his Berkshire shares — which make up over 99% of his net worth — to the Gates Foundation and four family foundations over the past 16 years.

Buffett announced earlier this month that he plans to donate the rest of his Berkshire shares — worth about $140 billion today — to his family foundations within the next eight years or so, and hopes his three children will distribute all of them to good causes by the end of 2034.

Musk's net worth stood at $709 billion at Monday's close, per the Bloomberg Billionaires Index. It briefly crossed $1 trillion last month after SpaceX went public, but the aerospace company's stock has roughly halved in price from its peak.

If Musk pledges to give even $100 billion to good causes, and follows through on that commitment, he would join the likes of Buffett and Bill Gates in the ranks of history's greatest philanthropists.

Banking on a future of abundance

Musk has said repeatedly in recent months that advances in AI, energy, and robotics will drive down the cost of everything from food and housing to healthcare and education.

He's said that "saving for retirement will be irrelevant" if he's right, and recommended people stop "squirreling money away" if they're retiring in 10 or 20 years as their nest eggs "won't matter."

The serial entrepreneur has also said that government checks will be the "best way" to deal with job losses from AI, as technological progress will make producing goods and services so cheap that paying a "universal high income" won't cause inflation.

Business Insider has reviewed hundreds of responses to Musk's comments on X and Facebook, and on personal finance, AI, and Musk-focused subreddits, and has found widespread disbelief in his vision of a world where money has no value.

Pledging to give away a huge sum could be Musk's way of showing he's serious, and perhaps convincing others that he's right.

content_html_zh:
作者：Theron Mohamed 您目前正在关注该作者！ 想要取消关注吗？ 通过电子邮件中的链接取消订阅。

埃隆·马斯克即将给我们留下他对沃伦·巴菲特的最佳印象吗？

这位特斯拉和 SpaceX 的首席执行官开玩笑说，他可能会将部分财富用于公益事业，以表明他真正相信技术将创造如此丰富的财富，以至于金钱将变得无关紧要。

诺贝尔经济学家达龙·阿西莫格鲁（Daron Acemoglu）在最近的一次采访中回应马斯克对后财富世界的预测，提出了“把钱花在嘴上的机会”之后，马斯克提出了这一前景。

这位麻省理工学院的资深教授写道：“如果钱在 2036 年不再重要，为什么不承诺在 2036 年之前将目前约 1 万亿美元的财富捐赠给慈善机构呢？”

阿西莫格鲁表示，这样做将“以极大的可信度确立”马斯克对“人工智能和技术力量”的信念，并缓解人们对“亿万富翁和万亿富翁的政治和社会影响力”的广泛担忧。

该帖子引发了 X 上的激烈争论，导致马斯克在几个小时后发表了看法。 “我实际上要做一些这样的事情！” 他写道。

我实际上打算按照这些思路做一些事情！——Elon Musk (@elonmusk) 2026 年 7 月 27 日

马斯克尚未详细说明他的计划。 特斯拉、SpaceX 和 X 没有立即回应《商业内幕》的置评请求。

借鉴巴菲特的剧本

如果马斯克承诺在未来十年左右的时间内将其大部分财富捐给慈善机构，那么他将与巴菲特展开竞争。

2010 年，巴菲特与他人共同发起了“捐赠誓言”，鼓励其他超​​级富豪与他一起签署该誓言，并承诺将大部分财富捐献给公益事业。

这位传奇投资者兼伯克希尔哈撒韦公司首席执行官在过去 16 年里将其伯克希尔哈撒韦公司约 60% 的股票（占其净资产的 99% 以上）捐赠给了盖茨基金会和四个家族基金会。

巴菲特本月早些时候宣布，他计划在未来八年左右的时间内将剩余的伯克希尔股票（目前价值约 1,400 亿美元）捐赠给他的家族基金会，并希望他的三个孩子在 2034 年底前将所有股票分配给慈善事业。

根据彭博亿万富翁指数，截至周一收盘，马斯克的净资产为 7090 亿美元。 上个月 SpaceX 上市后，该公司的股价曾短暂突破 1 万亿美元，但这家航空航天公司的股价已较峰值大约减半。

如果马斯克承诺为公益事业捐赠 1000 亿美元，并兑现这一承诺，他将与巴菲特和比尔·盖茨等人一起跻身历史上最伟大慈善家的行列。

寄托于富裕的未来

马斯克近几个月多次表示，人工智能、能源和机器人技术的进步将降低从食品、住房到医疗保健和教育的一切成本。

他表示，如果他是对的，“为退休储蓄将无关紧要”，并建议人们在 10 或 20 年后退休时停止“存钱”，因为他们的储蓄“并不重要”。

这位连续创业者还表示，政府支票将是应对人工智能造成的失业的“最佳方式”，因为技术进步将使生产商品和服务变得如此便宜，以至于支付“普遍高收入”不会导致通货膨胀。

《商业内幕》审查了数百条对马斯克在 X 和 Facebook、个人理财、人工智能和以马斯克为中心的 Reddit 子版块上的评论的回应，发现人们普遍不相信他所设想的金钱没有价值的世界。

承诺捐出一大笔钱可能是马斯克表明自己认真的方式，或许还能让其他人相信他是对的。
